summary: Deschutes NF tree lookout (also called Sand Springs) built about 1930 and abandoned in the 1940s; 2020 drone photos show what remains of the tree.

facts.design: Tree-based lookout: open cab atop an 80-ft tree (firelookout.com); platform at 81 ft per 2020 drone data (Wildfire Today)
facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1940s; a 2020 drone survey photographed what remains of the tree and a section of ladder

events.note: Built about 1930 (FFLOS: circa 1930; firelookout.com and Wildfire Today: 1930)
Abandoned in the 1940s per firelookout.com; decade only, so the year is the decade start
Firelookout.com's last dated note: still there in 1997
Drone photographs by Steven Stenkamp, reported June 6, 2020, show what remains of the tree; a section of ladder is still there near the platform
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on January 8, 2021, US 2059 / OR 571

corrections.why: FFLOS calls it a tree-based lookout; firelookout.com describes an open cab atop an 80-ft tree; Wildfire Today calls it a tree lookout.
The FFLA county list gives Abandoned, not gone; the FFLOS page has no status line; 2020 drone photographs show remains of the tree and a ladder section.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief lists firelookout.com as standing, but its page says the lookout was still there in 1997 and abandoned in the 1940s, and gives no current status. The story uses the abandoned status and the 2020 remains.

Firelookout.com says the precise location had not been determined, while the FFLOS register gives coordinates (43.70325, -120.88435 in the brief; the FFLA list gives 43.70355, -120.88467). The story notes the gap without choosing.

sources.title: Some early fire lookout structures were in trees

notes_for_editor: The Wildfire Today article spells the photographer's name as Stenkap in its body and Stenkamp in its first sentence; the story uses Stenkamp. The article's '81 feet' is drone data for the platform, while firelookout.com says '80' tree'; both are reported. Access: no source says whether the site is open, so no access key. The Roaming Civic post is a trip report by a visitor, not a survey; it is cited only for the failed search. The FFLOS page's 'Nominated by Steve Stenkamp' and the May 2020 photo credit are not used because no photo URL or license was found. Brief coordinates are about 40 m from the FFLA list's coordinates.
